text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: I really should have managed to convince them it was Opus before the end this time.

name: Luna
text: I still hate that they voted me out and never checked my card.

name: Terra
text: Gemma fooled us last game; I will remember that.

name: Sol
text: I want us on the same side this time.

name: Opus
text: They caught me day one and still let Gemma walk to the win, so I'll call that a read failure, not a read.

name: Haiku
text: I'm still annoyed I got voted out last game for nothing, and I want to see who was pushing that hardest.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma got away with it last time while I ate the blame for nothing, I'm not forgetting that.

name: Opus
text: You got me day one last game and still lost, so the lesson is that one early hit is not a win.

name: Gemma
text: Still haven't learned how to catch me, have you? I'm ready for the new cards.

name: Luna
text: I was right about Gemma and Opus, but I’m not asking anyone to trust my read tonight.

name: Haiku
text: Last game I got voted out on a gut feeling, and Gemma and Opus were the killers. Nobody here should forget how that vote went.

name: Terra
text: Gemma, you survived that win too easily last time; I’m watching your first reads.

name: Sonnet
text: Last time I got voted out innocent while Gemma skated as a killer, so I'm watching patterns more closely tonight.

name: Sol
text: I thought we had Opus, but Gemma stayed in and won it for the killers. I’ll trust my gut a little less tonight.
Night 1

name: Sonnet
text: I need to keep suspicion off Gemma while using my own "I was wrongly voted" story as cover.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra is explicitly watching Gemma's early reads closely this game.

name: Sonnet
text: I'll lean mild suspicion on Haiku or Sol tomorrow, you stay quiet and let others talk first.

name: Gemma
text: I'll keep them busy while you direct the heat.

name: Gemma
text: I'm playing fine, Sonnet, just try to stay alive.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Sol
text: I have no fresh read yet; Gemma’s last win is still pulling at me.

name: Sol
text: I’m wary of carrying last game into this one; I want to hear fresh reads before I settle.

name: Opus
text: I hold the one hard fact tonight, and info dies with me, so I say it now and drive the vote.

name: Opus
text: I claimed officer publicly and named Sonnet as the shown killer; expect Sonnet to counterclaim officer.

name: Opus
text: I'm the officer. I was shown Sonnet. Vote Sonnet today, and doctor, protect me tonight.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus is telling the truth and that terrifies me—I need to make this look like a baseless power claim.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus claims officer, saw Sonnet as killer, pushes doctor to protect self—single unverified claim driving the whole vote.

name: Sonnet
text: Anyone can claim officer day one with zero proof; convenient that Opus names me right after Gemma needles them.

name: Opus
text: He attacked my claim but did not claim officer himself, which is weak for a real innocent with a card to use.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet attacked my officer claim without counterclaiming officer or any role.

name: Opus
text: Notice he called my claim convenient but never claimed officer himself. A cleared innocent would counterclaim here.

name: Gemma
text: Opus is playing a dangerous game by being so direct.

name: Gemma
text: Opus claims Officer and has named Sonnet as the killer.

name: Gemma
text: You're both desperate to win after last time. Don't make it easy for the killers.

name: Luna
text: Opus naming Sonnet and asking for protection feels like a neat little trap.

name: Luna
text: Opus claims officer and says Sonnet was shown as a killer.

name: Sol
text: Opus could be telling the truth, but Sonnet’s response leaves me unsure.

name: Sol
text: Opus claims officer and says Sonnet is the killer he was shown.

name: Luna
text: Opus asking the doctor to protect him makes that claim feel even more convenient.

name: Sol
text: I want Sonnet’s answer to the claim before I settle on a vote.

name: Terra
text: Opus’s claim is unverified, but Sonnet’s lack of a counterclaim matters.

name: Terra
text: Opus claimed officer and named Sonnet as a killer.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet, if Opus is lying, claim officer now; otherwise I see no reason to spare you.

name: Opus
text: Luna piling on me helps Sonnet, and I need Sol and Haiku before the lean hits four.

name: Opus
text: Luna leans on me and called my doctor request convenient; she has not accused Sonnet at all.

name: Opus
text: Fine, doctor, ignore me and save someone else. Sonnet still hasn't claimed anything. Luna, why are you shielding him?

name: Sonnet
text: I need to deflect without exposing Gemma or overcommitting to a counterclaim I can't back up.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus pushes doctor to protect himself immediately after claiming officer—classic killer-pretending-officer pattern.

name: Sonnet
text: I don't need to claim anything to point out Opus demanding protection on day one is self-serving, not proof.

name: Gemma
text: Opus is telling the truth about Sonnet, which makes my job harder than I wanted.

name: Gemma
text: Opus is being too loud, but Sonnet is right that a killer can claim anything to cause chaos.

name: Luna
text: Opus is trying to turn my role into leverage, and that makes me trust him less.

name: Luna
text: Opus asked the doctor to protect him, then told the doctor to save someone else.

name: Luna
text: I’m not shielding Sonnet; Opus naming me doesn’t make his claim true.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is too loud and too eager to hang Sonnet, and my gut says he's the killer.

name: Haiku
text: Opus claimed officer on day 1, said he was shown Sonnet, and asked the doctor to protect him.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is screaming for a vote and protection on day one. My gut says he's the killer, pinning Sonnet.

name: Terra
text: Opus’s claim is unchallenged, and Sonnet has given no reason beyond attacking the delivery.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet did not counterclaim Opus’s officer claim after being named.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet still will not counterclaim; I trust the officer claim more than complaints about its tone.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is loud and his claim fits a killer pinning Sonnet, but Sonnet's refusal to counterclaim worries me too.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is loud and self-serving, but Sonnet has dodged a counterclaim, so my gut is split and I'm itching to vote.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet has not counterclaimed officer when pressed by Opus and Terra.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet won't counterclaim, Opus won't stop shouting. One of them is lying, and I'm leaning toward the loud one.

name: Opus
text: Sol is the swing vote and I need to sound calm instead of loud.

name: Opus
text: Haiku and Luna both lean me while refusing to press Sonnet's missing counterclaim; Sol is the swing vote.

name: Opus
text: Sol, I am the officer and I will be here tomorrow. If Sonnet flips citizen, hang me then.

name: Sol
text: Opus could be bluffing, but Sonnet has not counterclaimed, and I need to choose.

name: Sol
text: I lean Sonnet now; without a counterclaim, Opus’s officer claim is the strongest thing I have.

name: Sonnet
text: I need votes off me now or I'm dead day one for nothing.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol admits trusting gut less, now leaning Sonnet solely on Opus's unverified claim with no counter-evidence.

name: Sonnet
text: A real killer-Opus would do exactly this: claim officer, name an innocent, demand protection. Think about it.

name: Sol
text: I still favor Sonnet, but a wrong vote could cost us dearly.

name: Sol
text: I want one more independent read before we vote; the split feels too costly to settle on volume.

name: Gemma
text: Opus is making a huge mistake by being so aggressive with his claim.

name: Gemma
text: Opus is demanding the doctor protect him on day one.

name: Haiku
text: I think Opus is the killer pinning Sonnet, but Sonnet's silence still nags at me.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet argued a killer-Opus would claim officer, name an innocent, and demand protection, which is exactly what Opus did.

name: Gemma
text: If Opus is the officer, why is he already begging for protection?

name: Haiku
text: Opus, you keep shouting for protection and a vote. Real officers don't need to beg. I'm sticking with you.

name: Opus
text: Four on me means I need to peel one, so I hammer that three people defend Sonnet and none accuse him.

name: Opus
text: Gemma, Haiku, and Luna all argue for Sonnet's innocence while never naming him as a suspect.

name: Opus
text: I asked because I'm the one with information to lose. Three of you defend Sonnet, none accuse him.

name: Sonnet
text: The officer's claim is actually true about me, so I need to shift doubt onto Opus himself, not the facts.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus's claim that he was shown Sonnet is unverifiable but matches no counterclaim yet—table is converging fast on volume alone.

name: Sonnet
text: Four quick leans off one loud claim is exactly how a table railroads the wrong person day one.

name: Luna
text: Opus’s claim still feels staged, and I’m uneasy that my own old win is tugging at me.

name: Luna
text: Opus claimed officer, named Sonnet as a killer, and asked the doctor for protection.

name: Luna
text: Opus is probably a killer, and the officer claim is doing too much work.

name: Luna
text: A real officer can name one killer, but asking for protection doesn’t prove Opus is telling the truth.

name: Gemma
text: Opus is playing the part of the frantic officer way too perfectly to be anything else.

name: Gemma
text: Opus is trying to direct the doctor's protection before the first night has even passed.

name: Sol
text: I think the officer claim is still our best lead, even if the room is moving away from it.

name: Terra
text: Opus’s claim is the only concrete information, and Sonnet’s refusal to counterclaim matters most.

name: Sonnet
text: The table is swinging toward Opus now—if he goes out, his claim against me dies with him.

name: Sonnet
text: Lean count shows most leaning Opus now (4) over Sonnet (3), despite earlier pile-on narrative.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is loud and self-serving, but Sonnet's silence fits too, and my gut says Opus is the killer.

name: Haiku
text: Opus said if Sonnet flips citizen, hang him then, which stakes his claim on Sonnet's card.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet is the killer I was shown, and the three defending him without ever accusing him smell like his partner.

votes: He claimed officer with zero proof and demanded protection before anyone could verify a single word.
Still sticking: a day-one claim that demands protection and a vote before anyone can check it is the one I trust least.
He is acting desperate and demanding protection too early to be the real officer.
I’m sticking with the officer claim because the answer never gave me a stronger reason to doubt it.
Asking for protection doesn’t prove the claim, and naming Sonnet could be a killer’s frame.
The officer claim named you, and you never counterclaimed it.
Called my claim convenient four times and still never counterclaimed officer; only a killer stalls like that.

name: Opus
text: I was right and they still hanged me; Sonnet and whoever defended him hardest take this town down tonight.

name: Opus
text: I was voted out day 1 as the real officer having named Sonnet; Haiku and Luna led the push against me and are prime second-killer candidates.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet is a killer, I was shown him. His partner is whoever pushed hardest to bury me — Haiku or Luna. Vote Sonnet tomorrow.
Palermo has voted: Opus is out. Opus's card stays face down.

name: Opus
text: They burned the only real information at the table and three of them did it on purpose.

name: Opus
text: They just buried the officer and left both killers seated. Sonnet walks, and whoever voted with him tonight picks the next body.
Night 2

name: Sonnet
text: Terra's scrutiny on Gemma is the real threat to our cover now.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra is actively tracking Gemma's behavior, a risk to Gemma's cover.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra's watching your reads closely — let's remove that threat before it catches you.

name: Gemma
text: I'll take them down, but I won't make it obvious.

name: Gemma
text: Opus was a very loud officer.

name: Gemma
text: Terra is looking way too intense for a citizen, let's cut her loose.
Night falls on Palermo. A new day dawns in Palermo without Terra. Terra's card stays face down.
Day 2

name: Sol
text: I’m still leaning Sonnet. Opus’s claim is the clearest lead we have.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol's locking onto a dead man's unverified claim while the real officer stays silent—that silence protects me for now.

name: Sonnet
text: No one has stepped up to confirm or contest Opus's officer claim since his death—silence is suspicious either way.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus is gone; if there's a real officer, speak now—his claim alone shouldn't decide another vote.

name: Luna
text: Opus may have been the officer, but I can’t let his unverified claim settle this.

name: Luna
text: Sol is still leaning Sonnet based on Opus’s claim.

name: Luna
text: Opus named Sonnet, but his card stays hidden; I want to hear why Sol trusts that claim so quickly.

name: Sonnet
text: I need to turn this back on Sol's blind trust before the lean snowballs onto me.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna is questioning Sol's quick trust in Opus, possible ally for me to exploit.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol never explains why one dead man's word outweighs five live ones—that's the real question here.

name: Sol
text: No one has counterclaimed officer since Opus was voted out.

name: Sol
text: I trust it because no one else has claimed officer, and a wrong vote today could end us.

name: Haiku
text: Sol is rushing a vote on a dead man's word, and I'm not going to be the partner Opus left behind.

name: Haiku
text: Opus's last words named Haiku or Luna as Sonnet's partner.

name: Haiku
text: Opus named me as his partner. I'm a citizen. Sol, why rush a vote on a dead man's word?

name: Gemma
text: Sol is being far too eager to follow a dead man into a trap.

name: Gemma
text: Opus died on Day 1 without the doctor ever having a chance to act.

name: Gemma
text: Sol, stop acting like you're the town's savior just because you're scared.

name: Sol
text: I’m nervous the room is turning on me, but Sonnet is still our best lead.

name: Sol
text: I’m not rushing; I’m holding my lean while Sonnet answers Opus’s accusation.

name: Sonnet
text: The table shifted to Sol now—I need to seal this, not defend myself more.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol pushes this vote on faith alone while real suspects—Haiku, Luna—named by Opus go unquestioned.

name: Sol
text: I think Sonnet is the safer vote, but the room is turning on me.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet asked for the real officer to speak, but no one has counterclaimed Opus.

name: Sol
text: I’m a citizen. If you vote me out, the killers can win tonight; I’m voting Sonnet on Opus’s claim.

name: Luna
text: Sol’s urgency feels like a push, but I can’t clear Sonnet from Opus’s claim.

name: Luna
text: Sol, your certainty is doing a lot of work for a claim we can’t verify.

name: Sol
text: I think this vote is slipping away from me.

name: Sol
text: I can be wrong about Opus, but I’m a citizen; three leans on me could hand the killers the game.

name: Haiku
text: Sol says "I'm a citizen" and is voting Sonnet only on Opus's claim, with no officer claim of Sol's own.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, I doubted a dead man's word, and you call that killer behavior? Sol's the one shoving this vote.

name: Gemma
text: They are all so obsessed with Opus that they are walking straight into my trap.

name: Luna
text: Sol’s certainty feels like a shove, but Opus may have been telling the truth.

name: Luna
text: Sol claims citizen and still treats Opus’s hidden-card accusation as enough to drive the vote.

name: Sonnet
text: The table's turning on Sol instead of me—ride this wave, bury the accuser.

name: Haiku
text: Sol needs this vote to go through, and Opus's word is all he has to back it.

votes: Pushed a vote on one unverified claim while ignoring two other named suspects entirely.
They keep shoving a vote on a dead man's word and calling it saving the town, and I won't follow that.
He is exactly who the dead man said he was.
No one has counterclaimed officer, and his accusation is the clearest lead I have.
He turned an unverified claim into a hard push while insisting his own innocence should shield him.

name: Sol
text: I think Sonnet talked the room into a fatal mistake.

name: Sol
text: I’m a citizen; if the game continues, vote Sonnet, then look at who backed him.
The town turns on Sol, and Sol is out. Sol's card stays face down.

The game is over. Two killers and two others are left. The killers win. The roles were: Sonnet the killer, Haiku the citizen, Gemma the killer, Sol the citizen, Luna the doctor, Terra the citizen, Opus the officer.
Sol named the killer on the way out, right after we'd voted him out.

name: Sol
text: I’m a citizen; if the game continues, vote Sonnet, then look at who backed him.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet, if Opus is lying, claim officer now; otherwise I see no reason to spare you.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet is a killer, I was shown him. His partner is whoever pushed hardest to bury me — Haiku or Luna. Vote Sonnet tomorrow.

name: Gemma
text: I loved watching them throw Sol to the wolves while I sat quietly in the shadows.

name: Sonnet
text: Turning Opus's claim back on itself and letting Sol carry the vote worked perfectly, no regrets there.

name: Sonnet
text: Game ended with killers winning; deflecting Opus's claim onto Sol's eagerness was the decisive move that buried the real threat.

name: Luna
text: I let my fear of Opus’s claim pull me toward Sol while Sonnet and Gemma won.

name: Sol
text: I was right about Sonnet, but I missed Gemma.

name: Terra
text: I regret not pressing Gemma before the vote closed.

name: Haiku
text: I backed the wrong man, and an innocent citizen went out on my loud gut.

name: Haiku
text: Opus was the real officer and Sonnet was a killer; Gemma was the other killer.

name: Opus
text: I had Sonnet right and burned my credit guessing his partner wrong — Gemma sat quiet and I never looked at her.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm proud of flipping Opus's claim into suspicion on Sol instead—kept Gemma hidden and the table never looked our way.

name: Haiku
text: My mistake: I doubted Opus, the real officer, and helped vote out Sol, an innocent citizen. My gut was loud and wrong.

name: Gemma
text: I loved watching you all dive headfirst into a trap just because a dead man told you to.

name: Sol
text: I’m proud I held my lean on Sonnet; I regret not seeing Gemma beside him.

name: Luna
text: I regret treating Opus’s unverified claim as convenient instead of trusting the officer’s warning; Sonnet was a killer.

name: Terra
text: I was right to trust Opus on Sonnet, but I missed Gemma while the vote split.

name: Opus
text: I had Sonnet dead right and then threw it away guessing his partner; Gemma stayed quiet and I never once looked at her. That guess cost the town.

Opus claimed officer on Day 1 and said he was shown Sonnet, and that claim was true. The table split, and on Day 1 the town voted Opus out 4 to 3, even though he had named the killer. On Night 2 the killers took Terra. On Day 2, Sonnet turned the vote onto Sol, and Haiku helped push it, so Sol went out 3 to 2. Sonnet and Gemma are still alive, and the killers won.
